result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) family for GAMLSS. twitter-card: title: >- [ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) family for GAMLSS. title: >- [ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) family for GAMLSS. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) family for GAMLSS. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L325-L685){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial(theta=1.0) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial` combines the two departures from plain `Poisson` counts that are most common in practice: overdispersion (variance exceeding the mean, as in `NegativeBinomial`) and structural excess zeros (as in `ZeroInflatedPoisson`). It is appropriate for count data where, even after allowing for a mixture of structural and sampling zeros, the remaining positive counts are still more variable than a Poisson model would predict — for example, healthcare utilization counts, insurance claim frequencies, or ecological abundance data with many true absences plus overdispersed non-zero counts. `mu` (the NB mean) and `pi` (the zero-inflation probability) are modeled as smooth functions of covariates through `GAMLSS`, while the overdispersion parameter `theta` is fixed at construction rather than estimated per observation. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [theta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Negative binomial size (overdispersion) parameter, must be positive. Larger values mean less overdispersion (`theta -> infinity` recovers `ZeroInflatedPoisson`); smaller values mean more overdispersion among the non-structural-zero counts. Unlike `mu` and `pi`, `theta` is a single fixed value shared across all observations rather than modeled by a smooth predictor. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Two distributional parameters are modeled, each with its own link: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \log(\mu), \qquad g_{\pi}(\pi) = \log\!\left(\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right). $$ The probability mass function is a mixture of a point mass at zero and a Negative Binomial distribution using the mean-size parameterization (`Var(NB) = mu + mu^2/theta`): $$ P(Y = 0) = \pi + (1-\pi)\, \mathrm{NB}(0 \mid \mu, \theta), \qquad P(Y = k) = (1-\pi)\, \mathrm{NB}(k \mid \mu, \theta) \quad \text{for } k > 0, $$ where $$ \mathrm{NB}(k \mid \mu, \theta) = \binom{k+\theta-1}{k} \left(\frac{\theta}{\theta+\mu}\right)^{\theta} \left(\frac{\mu}{\theta+\mu}\right)^{k}. $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS for overdispersed count data with excess zeros: ::: {#4625cc28 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.exp(0.5 + 0.4 * np.sin(x)) pi = expit(-1.0 + 0.8 * np.cos(x)) theta = 2.0 is_structural_zero = rng.uniform(size=n) < pi counts = rng.negative_binomial(theta, theta / (theta + mu)) y = np.where(is_structural_zero, 0, counts).astype(float) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "pi": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial(theta=theta), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial(theta=2, mu=log, pi=logit) N obs: 300 Global deviance: 911.2129 AIC: 921.0281 BIC: 939.2047 Log-likelihood: -455.6064 Converged: True (3 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 2.00 Smooth 1: edf = 1.00 --- pi --- EDF total: 2.91 Smooth 1: edf = 1.91 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [parameter_names](#parameter_names){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Names of the distributional parameters modeled by this family. | | [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the (negative) second derivative of the log-likelihood. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L554-L591){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature d2l_dtheta2( param, y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific working weight used by `GAMLSS`'s Fisher-scoring updates for the zero-inflated negative binomial model, computed separately for zero and positive observations and floored at `_EPS` to keep weights strictly positive. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weight for `param`. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the first derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to a parameter. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L513-L552){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature dl_dtheta( param, y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific score function for the zero-inflated negative binomial model, combining the derivative of the `NB(0 | mu, theta)` probability weighted by the mixture for zero observations with the ordinary negative binomial score $\partial \ell / \partial \mu = (y - \mu) / (\mu (1 + \mu/\theta))$ for positive observations. For `pi` the score reflects the same zero/positive split as in `ZeroInflatedPoisson.dl_dtheta`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to differentiate with respect to, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Generate starting values for `mu` and `pi` before the first IRLS iteration. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L628-L652){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Sets `mu` to the mean of the strictly positive observations (or 1.0 if none are positive) for every observation, and sets `pi` to half the observed fraction of zeros, clipped to `[0.01, 0.5]`. The fixed overdispersion parameter `theta` is not part of the returned dictionary since it is not estimated per observation. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Initial values for `"mu"` and `"pi"`, each broadcast to the shape of `y`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Map a distributional parameter from its natural scale to the link scale. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L434-L455){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link( param, values, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies the log link $\eta = \log(\mu)$ for `mu` (clamped away from zero via `_MU_FLOOR`), and the logit link $\eta = \log(\pi / (1-\pi))$ for `pi` (clamped away from 0 and 1). The overdispersion parameter `theta` is fixed and has no link. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to transform, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Transformed values on the link (linear predictor) scale. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the derivative of the link function with respect to the natural parameter. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L479-L501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_derivative( param, values, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns $d\eta/d\mu = 1/\mu$ for `mu` and $d\eta/d\pi = 1/(\pi(1-\pi))$ for `pi`, using the same clamping applied in `link`, for use by `GAMLSS`'s IRLS fitting routine. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Derivative of the link function evaluated at `values`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Map a distributional parameter from the link scale back to its natural scale. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L457-L477){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_inverse( param, eta, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the inverse of `link`: $\mu = e^{\eta}$ (clipped to $[-30, 30]$ before exponentiating to avoid overflow) for `mu`, and $\pi = \mathrm{expit}(\eta)$ for `pi`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to transform, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values on the link scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the total log-likelihood under the zero-inflated negative binomial model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L593-L626){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature log_likelihood( y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Evaluates $$ \ell = \sum_{i: y_i = 0} \log\!\big(\pi_i + (1-\pi_i)\, \mathrm{NB}(0 \mid \mu_i, \theta)\big) + \sum_{i: y_i > 0} \Big[\log(1-\pi_i) + \log \mathrm{NB}(y_i \mid \mu_i, \theta)\Big], $$ where $\mathrm{NB}(\cdot \mid \mu, \theta)$ is the negative binomial probability mass function in the mean-size parameterization with the fixed `theta`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"` for each observation. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw a random sample of counts from the fitted zero-inflated NB model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L654-L682){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( params, rng, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each observation, flips a `pi`-weighted coin to decide whether it is a structural zero; observations that are not structural zeros are drawn from a negative binomial distribution with the fixed `theta` and success probability `theta / (mu + theta)`, so a sampled value can still be zero even when it was not selected as a structural zero. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"` for each observation to simulate. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Random number generator exposing `uniform` and `negative_binomial` methods, such as a `numpy.random.Generator`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, one per row of `params`. :::
